note: Curated X post summaries (live API unavailable or unpaid). Follow accounts below for newest posts.

items.title: The Hindu
items.summary: @the_hindu reports that the death toll and number of missing in the Nepal floods keep rising, with water levels in Bhotekoshi up again this morning and tunnel rescues still underway.

items.title: The Kathmandu Post
items.summary: Families are arriving in Pokhara to look at photos of the 102 bodies recovered from the Bhotekoshi flood, with more than a thousand relatives already there. @kathmandupost notes a help desk offering free support with reports and transport.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: @NDRRMA_Nepal shared a list of people injured in the Rasuwa Bhotekoshi/Trishuli floods who are currently being treated in Kathmandu hospitals or have already been discharged.

items.title: Embassy of India Beijing
items.summary: After the floods and mudslides in Tibet, authorities there have set up two English hotlines for families trying to reach information on missing foreign nationals. Call 0086-891-6817165 or 0086-183-0802-6705 anytime. @EOIBeijing

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: @NDRRMA_Nepal shared a short update on the search, rescue and relief work for the Bhotekoshi flood, with details as of 9am on 14 Bhadra 2083.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: @NDRRMA_Nepal posted details of the men rescued today.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: @NDRRMA_Nepal shared a list of foreign citizens rescued today, August 29. Families can check the attached details in their post.

items.title: MoFA Nepal
items.summary: @MoFANepal says 626 bodies have been recovered from the Bhote Koshi flood, with about 2400 people still unaccounted for. Over 4450 have been rescued so far, including more than 187 foreign nationals, and searches are continuing.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: Hospitals in Kathmandu are treating people injured in the disaster who were brought there for care. @NDRRMA_Nepal shared the list with @moha_nepal.

items.title: MoFA Nepal
items.summary: After the flash floods along the Bhote Koshi River on 26 August, @MoFANepal reports 538 bodies recovered so far, with 511 people from 33 countries still missing while search and rescue teams keep working. Families can contact their emergency line at +977-9744441227 or +977-9744441228.

items.title: The Kathmandu Post
items.summary: Families searching for relatives missing after the floods may find bodies from Rasuwa and Nuwakot turning up far downstream, with morgues in Chitwan and Pokhara under strain. @kathmandupost

items.title: The Kathmandu Post
items.summary: In Nuwakot’s flooded villages, some families are still waiting for relief while searches for missing relatives and buried homes go on days after the Bhotekoshi surge. @kathmandupost

items.title: MoFA Nepal
items.summary: Families can reach Nepal’s foreign ministry @MoFANepal emergency control room for help with the Bhote Koshi flash flood in Rasuwa. Call or message +977-9744441227 or +977-9744441228 (7am–10pm) or email emergency@mofa.gov.np.

items.title: NDTV
items.summary: @ndtv shared a ground report from Rasuwa with Sikta Deo and Ranveer Singh, showing the debris and washed-out markets along the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli after the glacier flow. For the latest casualty numbers, check with NDRRMA.

items.title: The Rising Nepal
items.summary: @therising_np is reporting from the ground between Dhunge Bazaar, Trishuli, and Devighat, where people had only minutes to leave after the alert around 8:55am, with their journalists alongside the rescue teams.

items.title: MEA India
items.summary: Families with relatives in Nepal can reach @MEAIndia’s special control room for the floods at +91-11-23088718 or +91-11-23088719, or on WhatsApp at +91-9968291988 or situationroom@mea.gov.in.

items.title: NDRRMA Nepal
items.summary: @NDRRMA_Nepal is posting updates on rescue and coordination efforts for the Bhotekoshi and Rasuwa flash flood on their official portals. Families can check there for the latest information.

items.title: Nepal Police HQ
items.summary: @NepalPoliceHQ says their database has the official lists of people found, missing, or unidentified after the floods, and families should check there rather than unofficial posts.

items.title: Embassy of India Kathmandu
items.summary: The Indian embassy in Kathmandu (@IndiainNepal) is working with Nepalese authorities on search and rescue for Indian nationals affected by the flash floods in Rasuwa and Bhotekoshi. Families can contact the MEA control room or the embassy for help.

items.title: Parshuram Kaphle
items.summary: @journoprk passes along a Nepali journalist’s take on the Rasuwa and Bhote Koshi flash flood, noting that early warnings from across the northern border seem to have fallen short.
